title: Pin federated entries' resolved skills subtree, not just the tag name
description: check-federated-pins.mjs answers 'does v0.6.0 resolve and declare 0.6.0', not 'does v0.6.0 still contain the bytes we verified'. Federated entries pin by tag NAME, which is mutable: a tag can be repointed at different content and every consumer silently follows it. That is not theoretical -- lore-cli and quest-cli both had v0.6.0 deleted and recreated 2026-09-10/11 (OMARK-43), and the no-edit property that saved us there is the same mutability that would hide a real drift. A tag recreated with genuinely drifted skill content passes CI green today. Fix: record the resolved skills/ subtree SHA per federated entry and fail when it moves, keeping the no-edit property for legitimate re-tags whose content is unchanged. Raised independently by lore-cli's session and by this one.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Record the resolved skills/ subtree SHA per federated v-pin in a sidecar file, NOT as a new key in marketplace.json -- that file is consumed by Claude Code against its own marketplace schema and must not carry fields the loader does not expect.

Checker resolves the chain live (tag ref -> tag object -> commit -> root tree -> skills subtree) and fails when the resolved subtree differs from the recorded one, with a message naming a repoint as the cause rather than just printing two SHAs.
A ref bump with no baseline update fails, and a v-pin with no baseline at all fails -- so the baseline cannot silently go stale, nor be skipped for a newly added entry.
Regression test proves the guard actually fails on a repointed tag, a stale baseline, and a missing baseline -- offline against a local fixture server, same shape as the existing v0.4.3 test.

Wired into CI next to the existing pin check. The offline regression test runs unconditionally; the live content check must also run where it can actually catch a repoint, which is NOT only on marketplace.json changes -- a tag moves without this repo changing at all.
